title: Chicken in Green Pumpkin Seed Sauce
description: Chicken simmered in a bright green sauce of toasted pumpkin seeds, tomatillos and roasted poblano, a nutty central-Mexican pipián that tastes earthy and herbal rather than fiery.

ingredients.item: white onion, half quartered for poaching and half chopped for the sauce
garlic, divided (2 whole for poaching, 3 for the sauce)

ingredients.note: sold raw and shelled at health-food or baking-supply stores in Manila; do not use salted roasted pepitas
or substitute drained canned tomatillos

ingredients.item: poblano pepper, roasted, peeled and seeded
ingredients.note: green bell pepper is a milder, less authentic stand-in if poblano is unavailable
for a milder family pot, omit and pass hot sauce at the table
a traditional thickener for the sauce

steps: Poach the chicken in the water with the quartered onion half and 2 whole garlic cloves, 25-30 minutes until cooked through; lift out the chicken and reserve 2 cups of the broth.
Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry skillet over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until they puff and start to pop, 4-5 minutes; watch closely so they don't scorch, then cool.
Simmer the tomatillos and serrano in a small pot of water 8-10 minutes until they turn from bright to olive green and soften; drain.
Blend the toasted pumpkin seeds, cooked tomatillos and serrano, roasted poblano, chopped onion, remaining garlic, romaine, cilantro and 1.5 cups of the reserved broth until completely smooth.
Heat the lard in a wide pot over medium heat, pour in the blended sauce carefully as it will spatter, and stir constantly for the first 3-4 minutes so it doesn't scorch or split.
Simmer the sauce uncovered, stirring occasionally, 10-12 minutes until it thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon and deepens to olive green.
Add the chicken pieces, season with salt, cover and simmer gently 10 minutes to heat through without letting the sauce boil hard.
Serve hot over rice with lime wedges.
tips: Keep the heat gentle once the sauce is in the pot; pumpkin-seed sauces can split into oil and solids if boiled hard.
Toast the pepitas slowly over low heat, they turn bitter if scorched.
nutritionNote: Pumpkin seeds add plant protein, iron and healthy fats to the lean chicken; serve with rice or corn tortillas and skip extra oil since the sauce is already rich.

source.name: Mexico in My Kitchen (Mely Martinez, Mole Verde / Pipián Verde)

title: Picadillo
description: Ground beef simmered with potatoes, carrots and tomato until saucy, a homey everyday filling Mexican mothers make for tacos, stuffed peppers or simply spooned over rice.

ingredients.note: 80/20 lean-to-fat works best for flavor
or 1 cup canned crushed tomatoes
fresh or frozen, thawed
optional; more common in northern Mexican kitchens

steps: Heat the oil in a wide skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until soft, about 3 minutes.
Add the garlic and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the ground beef, breaking it up with a spoon, and cook until no longer pink, 6-8 minutes, draining off excess fat if the mix looks greasy.
Stir in the tomatoes, cumin and bay leaf, and cook 3-4 minutes until the tomatoes break down.
Add the potatoes, carrot and broth, bring to a simmer, cover, and cook 15 minutes until the vegetables are just tender.
Stir in the peas, season with salt and pepper, and simmer uncovered 5 minutes more until the sauce thickens slightly and clings to the meat.
Remove the bay leaf and serve warm with warm corn tortillas or rice.
tips: Dice the potatoes small and uniform so they finish cooking in the same time as the beef.
Picadillo is even better the next day and freezes well for a quick future dinner.
nutritionNote: A balanced one-pot mix of protein, potato starch and vegetables; drain the grease after browning fattier beef to keep the dish lighter.

title: Meatballs in Chipotle Broth
description: Rice-studded beef meatballs simmered in a smoky chipotle-tomato broth until tender, a nostalgic weeknight soup that Mexican kids grow up asking for by name.

ingredients.note: hierbabuena is traditional; cilantro is a fine substitute

ingredients.item: canned chipotle peppers in adobo, chopped
ingredients.note: start with 1 tbsp for a milder family pot; keep extra chipotle on the side for adults who want more heat

steps: Mix the ground beef, rice, egg, chopped onion, garlic, mint, salt and pepper in a bowl until just combined; don't overwork the mixture.
Roll into golf-ball sized meatballs, about 16 total, and set aside on a tray.
Blend the tomatoes, onion, garlic and chipotle with 1 cup of the broth until smooth.
Pour the blended sauce into a large pot, bring to a simmer, and cook 8-10 minutes until it deepens in color and loses its raw smell.
Add the remaining broth and bring to a gentle boil.
Carefully drop in the meatballs one at a time; simmer uncovered, without stirring too much, 25-30 minutes until cooked through and the rice inside is tender.
Season with salt and skim any foam from the surface.
Ladle into bowls, sprinkle with cilantro and serve with warm tortillas.
tips: Don't stir vigorously once the meatballs go in, let the broth do the work or they'll break apart.
The raw rice inside each meatball needs the full simmer time to cook through, so don't rush the last step.
nutritionNote: A protein-rich soup with rice already built in; round it out with a side salad or extra broth vegetables like chayote or carrot.

title: Crispy Rolled Chicken Tacos
description: Corn tortillas rolled tight around shredded chicken and fried until crackling-crisp, then finished with crema, salsa and queso fresco, festive party food that disappears fast at kids' birthdays.

ingredients.note: warm before rolling so they don't crack
optional; keeps rolls from unraveling while frying
or sour cream thinned with a little milk

ingredients.item: salsa, red or green, served on the side
ingredients.note: keep chile out of the kids' portion; offer salsa as a table condiment so each person adds their own heat

steps: Poach the chicken in the water with onion, garlic and salt 20 minutes until cooked through; cool and shred finely.
Warm the tortillas briefly on a dry griddle or wrapped in a damp towel so they roll without cracking.
Place 2-3 tablespoons of shredded chicken along one edge of each tortilla, roll tightly into a cigar shape, and secure with a toothpick if needed.
Heat 1.5 cups oil in a deep skillet to 180C (350F).
Fry the flautas in batches, seam-side down first, turning occasionally, until golden and crisp all over, 3-4 minutes per batch.
Drain on paper towels and remove the toothpicks.
Pile onto a platter over shredded lettuce and top with crema, queso fresco and diced tomato.
Serve immediately with salsa on the side so each person adds their own.
tips: Frying seam-side down first helps seal the roll before it can unravel in the oil.
Fry in small batches so the oil temperature doesn't drop, which keeps the tortillas crisp rather than greasy.
nutritionNote: A fried, crowd-pleasing party dish; balance the plate with the lettuce and tomato garnish and a side of beans rather than more fried food.

title: Tortilla Soup
description: A pasilla-tomato broth ladled over crisp fried tortilla strips and topped with avocado, cheese and crema, the soup nearly every Mexico City kitchen serves before the main course.

ingredients.item: corn tortillas, cut into thin strips
vegetable oil, for frying the tortillas

ingredients.note: dried pasilla sold by Mexican/Latin specialty importers online in Manila; substitute 1 ancho chile if unavailable
or sour cream thinned with milk

steps: Fry the tortilla strips in batches in the hot oil until crisp and golden, about 2 minutes; drain on paper towels and set aside.
Soak the pasilla chile in hot water 10 minutes until soft, then drain.
Blend the tomatoes, onion, garlic and softened pasilla until completely smooth.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a pot over medium heat, pour in the blended sauce, and cook, stirring, 8-10 minutes until it darkens and thickens.
Add the broth, bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer 10 minutes and season with salt.
Just before serving, divide the fried tortilla strips among bowls and ladle the hot broth over them so they stay crisp at the table.
Top with avocado, queso fresco and a drizzle of crema, with lime wedges alongside.
tips: Add the tortilla strips to the bowl last, always, or they turn soggy sitting in the broth.
The salsa base can be made a day ahead and refrigerated; fry the tortillas fresh right before serving.
nutritionNote: A light tomato-based broth; keep the fried tortilla strips and crema portions modest for a lighter bowl, or bake the strips instead of frying for less oil.

source.name: 196 Flavors (recipe validated by Mely Martinez of Mexico in My Kitchen)

title: Roasted Poblano Strips in Cream
description: Roasted poblano strips simmered in a light garlic cream with sweet corn, a mild, silky side dish or taco filling found on nearly every central Mexican comedor menu.

ingredients.note: fresh, frozen or canned and drained
or sour cream thinned with a little milk
optional, for a richer finish

steps: Char the poblanos directly over a gas flame or under a hot broiler, turning, until blackened all over.
Seal the charred peppers in a plastic bag or covered bowl for 10 minutes to steam, then rub off the skin under cool running water.
Remove the stems and seeds, then slice the peppers into thin strips.
Heat the oil or butter in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until soft and translucent, 4-5 minutes.
Add the garlic and corn and cook 2 minutes.
Stir in the poblano strips and cook 2-3 minutes to combine the flavors.
Lower the heat, stir in the crema and salt, and simmer gently 3-4 minutes until warmed through; do not boil hard or the crema can split.
Scatter with cheese if using and serve warm as a side or tortilla filling.
tips: Poblanos vary in heat from pepper to pepper; taste a small piece after roasting, and if a batch runs spicier than expected, add extra crema and corn to mellow it for the kids' plates.
nutritionNote: Vegetable-forward with real fiber from the peppers and corn; the cream and cheese add richness, so keep this a side rather than the main dish, or thin the crema with milk for a lighter version.

title: Zucchini with Corn
description: Mexican zucchini and sweet corn sauteed with onion, tomato and a touch of chile, a quick everyday vegetable side that home cooks like Mely Martinez say they could eat daily.

ingredients.note: deseed for milder, or omit entirely for a fully mild pot
regular green zucchini is a close substitute
fresh off the cob is traditional; frozen or canned works too
optional garnish

steps: Heat the oil in a wide skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until translucent, 3 minutes.
Add the garlic and chile and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the diced zucchini and corn and cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the chopped tomatoes, cover, and cook 8-10 minutes until the zucchini is tender but not mushy and the tomatoes have broken down into a light sauce.
Uncover, season with salt, and simmer 2-3 minutes more to let any extra liquid evaporate.
Scatter with queso fresco if using and serve warm as a side, or spoon over rice for a light meal.
tips: Don't overcook the zucchini, it should still hold its shape; cut it into even pieces so it cooks at the same rate as the corn.
nutritionNote: A fiber- and vitamin-rich vegetable side that's naturally low in fat; a good way to get the kids eating vegetables since the corn sweetness balances the zucchini.

title: Green Chilaquiles
description: Fried tortilla chips simmered briefly in a tangy tomatillo-serrano salsa until just softened, topped with crema, queso fresco and a fried egg, the classic Mexican breakfast for using up yesterday's tortillas.

ingredients.note: or 1 pack (200 g) plain tortilla chips; day-old tortillas fried at home give the most authentic texture
omit if using store-bought chips
use 1, or deseed, for a milder pot; blend a small chile-free portion of sauce separately for the kids and keep the fuller-heat batch for the adults
optional
or sour cream thinned with milk

steps: If frying your own tortillas, cut into wedges and fry in batches in hot oil until crisp and golden; drain on paper towels. Skip this step if using store-bought chips.
Simmer the tomatillos and serrano chiles in a pot of water 10-12 minutes until they turn from bright to olive green and soften.
Blend the cooked tomatillos and chiles with the garlic, onion, cilantro, water and salt until smooth.
Pour the salsa into a wide skillet and simmer 5 minutes until it thickens slightly and loses its raw taste.
Add the tortilla chips to the skillet and gently fold them into the sauce, cooking just 1-2 minutes so they soften slightly but keep some bite; do not let them sit or they turn mushy.
Divide among plates immediately and top with a fried egg, queso fresco, crema and sliced onion.
tips: Chilaquiles wait for no one, fold the chips into the sauce only right before serving.
Make the salsa verde ahead and refrigerate it, then the dish comes together in minutes on a busy morning.
kidNote: Blend a small batch of the tomatillo sauce with just 1 seeded serrano (or none) for the kids' portion, and keep the fuller-heat sauce in a separate pan for the adults so each plate matches its own heat tolerance.
nutritionNote: Pair with a fried or scrambled egg for protein since the dish itself is mostly carbohydrate and fried tortilla; go light on the crema if serving often.

title: Garlic Shrimp
description: Shrimp seared fast in butter and a generous amount of garlic until golden and glossy, a coastal Mexican classic that comes together in the time it takes to cook rice.

ingredients.item: large shrimp, peeled and deveined, tails on

ingredients.note: yes, this much; the dish is meant to be heavily garlicky

ingredients.item: dried guajillo chile, seeded and thinly sliced
ingredients.note: optional, for color and mild warmth; omit entirely for the mildest version

steps: Season the shrimp with salt and set aside.
Melt the butter with the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the minced garlic and sliced guajillo, if using, and cook gently 1-2 minutes, stirring, until the garlic turns pale golden; watch closely, burnt garlic turns bitter.
Raise the heat to medium-high, add the shrimp in a single layer, and cook undisturbed 1-2 minutes until pink on the bottom.
Flip the shrimp and cook 1-2 minutes more until just opaque all the way through; do not overcook or they turn rubbery.
Remove from heat, stir in the lime juice, and toss to coat.
Scatter with parsley and serve immediately with lime wedges, rice and warm tortillas.
tips: Keep the garlic moving in the butter so it toasts evenly without burning.
Buy shrimp already peeled and deveined to keep this a genuine weeknight dish.
nutritionNote: Shrimp is lean and high in protein; this dish leans buttery, so balance the plate with rice, a green salad or steamed vegetables rather than more fat.

title: Beef and Vegetable Soup
description: Beef shank simmered for hours into a clear, deeply savory broth loaded with corn, cabbage, chayote and potato, the Sunday soup that feeds the whole family and leaves leftovers.

ingredients.item: beef shank or short ribs, bone-in
carrots, peeled and cut into chunks
chayote, peeled and cut into chunks
ingredients.note: substitute an extra potato or a small squash if chayote is unavailable
table-only, keep off the kids' bowls; serve alongside for adults who want it spicier

steps: Place the beef shank in a large pot with the water, quartered onion, garlic and salt; bring to a boil, skimming off any foam.
Reduce to a low simmer, cover partially, and cook 1.5 to 2 hours until the meat is very tender and starting to pull from the bone.
Add the corn, carrots, potatoes and tomatoes and simmer 20 minutes.
Add the chayote and cabbage wedges and simmer 15 minutes more.
Add the zucchini in the last 10 minutes of cooking so it doesn't turn to mush.
Taste the broth and adjust the salt.
Ladle the meat, vegetables and broth into deep bowls.
Serve with lime wedges, chopped cilantro, warm corn tortillas, and the whole serrano on the side for anyone who wants extra heat.
tips: This is a weekend project, the shank needs real time to turn tender and give its flavor to the broth, so start it early in the day.
Skim the fat off the surface once the broth cools slightly for a lighter final bowl.
nutritionNote: A well-rounded one-pot meal with protein, starch and several vegetables in a light broth; skim excess fat off the top before serving for a leaner bowl.
